rules.action: Review diagnostic data policy

rules.featureLoss: Optional diagnostic information is reduced. Home and Pro still send required diagnostic data.

rules.target: Cortana and web search in Start

rules.reason: Cortana has been retired; these legacy policies do not guarantee that every current Start search surface changes.
rules.featureLoss: Cortana and supported connected search results are disabled. Local file search remains available.

rules.action: Disable capture only if unused
rules.reason: Background game recording can be unnecessary when another capture tool is used.
rules.featureLoss: Windows game recording/capture is disabled; this setting does not uninstall Game Bar.

rules.action: Reduce visual effects if preferred
rules.reason: A visual preference; the effect on performance varies with the system.
rules.featureLoss: Window/taskbar animations and transparency are reduced. Sign-out may be needed.

rules.target: Ads and suggestions in Start / lock screen
rules.action: Reduce suggested content if unwanted
rules.reason: Uses the existing per-user ContentDeliveryManager settings; Windows builds may expose additional suggestion surfaces.
rules.featureLoss: Some Start/lock-screen suggestions and automatic suggested-app installation are disabled.

rules.action: Disable cross-device activity history if unused
rules.reason: Activity publishing and uploading are separate from clipboard history.
rules.featureLoss: Windows activity feed, publishing and uploading are disabled. Clipboard history is unchanged.

rules.action: Review apps that require location first
rules.reason: This is a machine-wide location policy and can affect apps beyond the current user.
rules.featureLoss: Windows and apps lose location access; location-dependent features may stop working.

rules.action: Keep automatic cleanup unless managing it yourself
rules.reason: Storage Sense manages temporary files and supported cloud content; disabling it is not a general performance optimization.
rules.featureLoss: Automatic Storage Sense cleanup stops; disk space must be managed manually.

rules.action: Prefer individual app settings when possible
rules.reason: The existing policy is machine-wide and is not a universal switch for desktop processes.
rules.featureLoss: Affected Windows apps lose background work and notifications; mail/sync may be delayed.

rules.action: Review notification needs before disabling
rules.reason: Notification banners include useful reminders and alerts, not only suggestions.
rules.featureLoss: App and Windows popup notifications are disabled for this user.

rules.action: Keep power management unless diagnosing a specific issue
rules.reason: Disabling background power throttling trades battery life/heat for background responsiveness.
rules.featureLoss: Background workloads may consume more power; no guaranteed foreground speed improvement.

rules.action: Show extensions and hidden files if useful
rules.reason: This changes Explorer's presentation; Pathweft's visibility toggle remains independent.
rules.featureLoss: Hidden files become visible and extensions are shown; files are not modified.

rules.action: Expose End task only if needed
rules.reason: End task forcibly ends an app and can discard unsaved work. Availability is build-dependent.
rules.featureLoss: Adds a destructive command to the Windows taskbar menu; no process is ended by applying the setting.

rules.action: Use only if the legacy menu is preferred
rules.reason: The legacy Explorer shell override is build-specific and does not change Pathweft's own menu.
rules.featureLoss: Explorer uses its classic context menu where supported; Explorer restart/sign-out may be needed.

rules.action: Change only to investigate sign-in behavior
rules.reason: Removing Explorer's startup delay can increase simultaneous disk/CPU contention at sign-in.
rules.featureLoss: Registered startup programs may compete for resources earlier. Tasks and services are unaffected.

rules.action: Disable saving Recall snapshots if unused
rules.reason: Relevant only to supported Copilot+ hardware/editions; setting a policy does not prove Recall is installed.
rules.featureLoss: Recall snapshot saving/analysis is disabled where the policy is supported; existing saved data is not removed here.

rules.action: Keep if using Outlook or Windows indexing
rules.reason: Everything's filename index does not replace Outlook or Windows content indexing.
rules.featureLoss: Windows/Outlook indexed search can become unavailable or slower.

rules.action: Keep unless diagnosing a reproducible issue
rules.reason: Preloading commonly used apps is not evidence of wasted memory.
rules.featureLoss: Windows application preloading/optimization is disabled.

rules.action: Keep crash reporting available
rules.reason: Error reporting supports problem diagnosis. Manual startup is different from Disabled.
rules.featureLoss: Windows error reporting and associated diagnostic collection are unavailable.

rules.action: Disable only if no fax functionality is used
rules.reason: A feature-specific service; not a general performance recommendation.
rules.featureLoss: Sending and receiving faxes through Windows stops.

rules.action: Disable only if offline maps are unused
rules.reason: Downloaded maps are a distinct feature with their own update needs.
rules.featureLoss: Downloaded maps management and updates stop.

rules.action: Keep disabled outside retail demonstrations
rules.reason: Used for retail demo configuration; a stopped/manual service does not consume continual CPU.
rules.featureLoss: Retail demonstration features are unavailable.

rules.action: Review management requirements first
rules.reason: Some management products use remote registry; low activity does not establish that it is unused.
rules.featureLoss: Remote registry access is unavailable; local registry access is unaffected.

rules.action: Review diagnostic and gaming consequences
rules.reason: Privacy and diagnostic choices can affect Feedback Hub and Xbox achievements; do not label it universally unnecessary.
rules.featureLoss: Connected diagnostics and dependent experiences can stop working.

rules.action: Review device-management requirements
rules.reason: Managed devices can depend on WAP push message routing.
rules.featureLoss: Some device-management push functionality may stop.

rules.action: Review printing requirements
rules.reason: Printer extension notifications are distinct from the print spooler.
rules.featureLoss: Printer extension notifications and dialogs may be unavailable.

rules.action: Remove only if unused
rules.reason: An optional game package for the current user.
rules.featureLoss: Solitaire is removed for this user; reinstall from Microsoft Store. App data may be lost.

rules.action: Remove only if unused

rules.action: Turn off local and remote agent connectors

rules.featureLoss: AI agents (for example Copilot) cannot use Windows agent connectors to act in apps or read app data.

rules.action: Turn off agent workspaces

rules.featureLoss: Agentic features that operate in a background agent workspace are unavailable.

rules.action: Turn off Notepad AI features

rules.action: Turn off Paint AI features

rules.featureLoss: Windows has less up-to-date compatibility data when it decides whether to offer a feature update, so upgrade blocks for incompatible apps may be detected later.

rules.featureLoss: Windows no longer prompts for feedback; Feedback Hub still works when opened.

rules.action: Turn off cloud clipboard sync
rules.reason: Sets the policy that stops clipboard items being synced through your Microsoft account to other devices.
rules.featureLoss: Copied items no longer appear on your other devices; local clipboard history keeps working.

rules.action: Turn off cloud content search for Microsoft and work accounts
rules.reason: Stops Windows search showing results from your OneDrive, Outlook and other Microsoft or work and school account content.
rules.featureLoss: Windows search shows only local results; open OneDrive or Outlook to search cloud content.

rules.action: Turn off search history on this device
rules.reason: Stops Windows search keeping your search history on this PC to improve results.
rules.featureLoss: Recent searches are not suggested in the search box.

rules.target: Web suggestions in the search box
rules.action: Turn off web suggestions in search
rules.reason: Sets the user policy that stops the Start and taskbar search box sending what you type to Bing for web suggestions.
rules.featureLoss: No Bing web results or suggestions in Start and taskbar search. File Explorer search may also stop suggesting recent search entries.

rules.action: Deny apps access to diagnostic information about other apps
rules.reason: Turns off the device-wide App diagnostics permission so apps cannot read information about your other running apps.
rules.featureLoss: Apps that show running-app or diagnostic information (for example some support tools) lose that data.

rules.action: Deny apps access to your account info
rules.reason: Turns off the device-wide Account info permission so apps cannot read your name, picture and other account details.
rules.featureLoss: Apps cannot show your account name or picture or prefill your details.

rules.action: Turn off the advertising ID by policy
rules.reason: Sets the machine policy that turns off the advertising ID for every account on this PC.
rules.featureLoss: Apps cannot use the advertising ID for personalised ads; the Settings switch is greyed out.

rules.action: Hide recently used files in File Explorer
rules.reason: Stops File Explorer Home and Quick access listing files you opened recently.
rules.featureLoss: Recent files no longer appear in File Explorer Home or Quick access.

rules.action: Hide frequently used folders in File Explorer
rules.reason: Stops File Explorer adding folders you use often to Quick access.
rules.featureLoss: Only folders you pin appear in Quick access.

rules.target: Cloud files in File Explorer Home
rules.action: Hide files from Office.com in File Explorer
rules.reason: Stops File Explorer Home showing recent files from your Microsoft account in the cloud.
rules.featureLoss: Cloud documents from Office.com no longer appear in File Explorer Home.

rules.action: Turn off Find My Device by policy
rules.reason: Stops Windows periodically reporting this device location for Find My Device.
rules.featureLoss: You cannot locate or lock a lost or stolen PC from your Microsoft account.

rules.action: Send no optional diagnostic data from Edge
rules.reason: Limits Edge diagnostic data to the required minimum and stops browsing data being used to personalise Microsoft services.
rules.featureLoss: Microsoft receives less Edge usage data; personalised ads and news based on browsing stop. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Turn off the Edge feedback feature
rules.reason: Removes the Send feedback command from Edge.
rules.featureLoss: You cannot send feedback to Microsoft from Edge. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Turn off similar-page suggestions when a page is not found
rules.reason: Stops Edge sending failed web addresses to a Microsoft service to suggest similar pages.
rules.featureLoss: Edge shows a plain error page without suggestions. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Turn off Microsoft consumer experiences
rules.reason: Sets the policy that stops Windows installing suggested third-party apps and showing consumer promotions.
rules.featureLoss: No automatically installed promoted apps or consumer suggestions. Microsoft documents that this policy is honoured only on Enterprise and Education editions.

rules.action: Turn off cloud optimised content
rules.reason: Sets the policy that stops Windows showing cloud-delivered content such as promoted Start and taskbar items.
rules.featureLoss: Windows experiences that depend on cloud-delivered content show defaults instead.

rules.target: Microsoft account notices in Settings and Start
rules.action: Turn off account-state content
rules.reason: Sets the policy that hides Microsoft account and Microsoft 365 promotion cards in Settings and Start.
rules.featureLoss: Account status cards and subscription offers no longer appear in Settings or the Start account menu.

rules.action: Turn off Widgets by policy
rules.reason: Sets the Allow widgets policy to off, removing the Widgets board and its taskbar button.
rules.featureLoss: The Widgets board with news, weather and feeds is unavailable.

rules.action: Turn off news and interests on the taskbar
rules.reason: Sets the policy that removes the Windows 10 news and interests taskbar feed.
rules.featureLoss: The weather and news feed on the Windows 10 taskbar is removed.

rules.action: Hide the Chat button
rules.reason: Removes the Chat (Microsoft Teams personal) button from the Windows 11 taskbar.
rules.featureLoss: No Chat button on the taskbar; Teams can still be opened if installed.

rules.action: Hide the Meet Now icon
rules.reason: Sets the user policy that removes the Skype Meet Now icon from the Windows 10 notification area.
rules.featureLoss: No Meet Now shortcut in the notification area.

rules.target: Remote app installs from the Store website
rules.action: Turn off Push to Install
rules.reason: Sets the policy that stops apps chosen on the Microsoft Store website or another device being installed on this PC automatically.
rules.featureLoss: Apps you pick on the Store website or another device are not pushed to this PC; install them here instead.

rules.target: Device apps and icons from the internet
rules.action: Stop downloading device metadata
rules.reason: Sets the policy that stops Windows downloading manufacturer apps, icons and information for devices you connect.
rules.featureLoss: New devices may show generic icons and their manufacturer companion apps are not installed automatically; drivers are unaffected.

rules.action: Turn off the Edge sidebar
rules.reason: Removes the Edge sidebar with its apps and Copilot entry point.
rules.featureLoss: The Edge sidebar and its apps are unavailable. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Turn off Edge shopping features
rules.reason: Stops Edge offering coupons, price comparison and cashback on shopping sites.
rules.featureLoss: No price comparison, coupons or cashback offers in Edge. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Skip the Edge first-run pages
rules.reason: Hides the welcome and sign-in pages Edge shows the first time it runs.
rules.featureLoss: Edge does not walk you through import and sign-in on first launch. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Stop Edge asking to be the default browser
rules.reason: Stops Edge checking and prompting to become the default browser.
rules.featureLoss: Edge never offers to make itself default; set defaults in Settings if you want Edge. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Turn off Edge feature recommendations
rules.reason: Stops Edge showing recommendations and promotional notifications for its features.
rules.featureLoss: Edge no longer suggests features or shows promotional pop-ups. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Hide Microsoft Rewards in Edge
rules.reason: Hides Microsoft Rewards offers and the Rewards entry in Edge.
rules.featureLoss: Rewards points offers are not shown in Edge. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.target: News on the Edge new tab page

rules.featureLoss: The Edge new tab page shows no news feed. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Hide Home in the navigation pane

rules.featureLoss: Home is no longer shown in the navigation pane; its content stays available by other routes.

rules.action: Hide Gallery in the navigation pane
rules.reason: Unpins Gallery from the File Explorer navigation pane for this user.
rules.featureLoss: Gallery is no longer shown in the navigation pane; its content stays available by other routes.

rules.action: Hide OneDrive in the navigation pane
rules.reason: Unpins OneDrive from the File Explorer navigation pane for this user.
rules.featureLoss: OneDrive is no longer shown in the navigation pane; its content stays available by other routes.

rules.target: Full path in the title bar
rules.action: Show the full folder path in the title bar
rules.reason: Shows the complete path of the current folder in the File Explorer window and taskbar title.
rules.featureLoss: None; titles become longer.

rules.action: Use check boxes to select items
rules.reason: Shows a check box beside files and folders in File Explorer to make multiple selection easier.
rules.featureLoss: None; check boxes appear on hover and selection.

rules.target: Folder windows in a separate process
rules.action: Launch folder windows in a separate process
rules.reason: Runs File Explorer windows in a process separate from the desktop and taskbar, so a crashing folder window does not take the taskbar with it.
rules.featureLoss: Uses somewhat more memory.

rules.action: Treat all folders as general items
rules.reason: Stops File Explorer inspecting folder contents to pick a Pictures, Music or Documents layout, which can slow large folders.
rules.featureLoss: Folders no longer get type-specific columns and views automatically. Views already remembered for a folder are kept until you reset them.

rules.action: Name new shortcuts without the "- Shortcut" suffix
rules.reason: Makes new shortcuts take the plain name of their target instead of adding "- Shortcut".
rules.featureLoss: None; existing shortcuts keep their names.

rules.action: Enable Win32 long path support
rules.reason: Lets applications that opt in use file paths longer than 260 characters.
rules.featureLoss: None for apps that do not opt in; File Explorer itself still has some limits.

rules.action: Hide the Recommended section in Start
rules.reason: Sets the user policy that removes the Recommended section of the Start menu.
rules.featureLoss: Start no longer lists recent files and recommended apps. Some Windows 11 builds and editions only partly honour this policy.

rules.action: Hide recently added apps in Start
rules.reason: Stops Start listing apps you installed recently.
rules.featureLoss: Newly installed apps are not highlighted in Start.

rules.action: Hide most used apps in Start
rules.reason: Stops Start listing the apps you use most.
rules.featureLoss: No Most used list in Start.

rules.action: Use the More pins Start layout
rules.reason: Gives pinned apps more room in Start by shrinking the Recommended area.
rules.featureLoss: Fewer recommendations are shown.

rules.action: Hide the mobile device pane in Start
rules.reason: Removes the Phone Link companion pane beside the Start menu.
rules.featureLoss: Your phone is not shown in Start; the Phone Link app still works.

rules.action: Show seconds in the taskbar clock
rules.reason: Adds seconds to the clock in the notification area.
rules.featureLoss: Slightly more power use on battery.

rules.action: Show taskbar buttons only on the display where the window is open
rules.reason: With several displays, each taskbar shows only the windows on its own display.
rules.featureLoss: The main taskbar no longer lists windows that are on other displays.

rules.action: Download updates over HTTP only, without peers
rules.reason: Sets the Delivery Optimization download mode policy to HTTP only, so this PC neither downloads updates from nor uploads them to other PCs.
rules.featureLoss: Updates come only from Microsoft servers, which can use more internet bandwidth on networks with several PCs. Updates themselves keep working.

rules.action: Turn on hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling
rules.reason: Lets a supported graphics card manage its own memory scheduling, which can reduce latency in games.
rules.featureLoss: Needs a restart and a supporting driver; with some drivers it causes stutter, black screens or app problems.

rules.action: Turn off Edge Startup Boost
rules.reason: Stops Edge starting at sign-in and staying in the background after you close it.
rules.featureLoss: Edge opens a little more slowly the first time. Edge shows "Your browser is managed by your organization" while any Edge policy is set.

rules.action: Exclude drivers from quality updates
rules.reason: Sets the policy that stops Windows Update installing driver updates together with quality updates.
rules.featureLoss: You must update device drivers yourself; fixes for hardware problems and some security fixes in drivers arrive only when you install them.

rules.action: Do not restart automatically while someone is signed in
rules.reason: Sets the policy that stops Windows Update restarting the PC on its own while a user is signed in.
rules.featureLoss: Installed updates, including security fixes, stay pending until you restart. Microsoft documents that this applies when automatic updates are configured to schedule installs.

rules.action: Adjust active hours automatically
rules.reason: Lets Windows set active hours from when you actually use the PC, so update restarts avoid those times.
rules.featureLoss: Manually chosen active hours are replaced by learned ones.

rules.action: Turn on network protection in block mode
rules.reason: Extends SmartScreen-style blocking of phishing, malware and command-and-control sites to every app, not only Microsoft Edge. Needs Microsoft Defender as the active antivirus.
rules.featureLoss: Connections to sites Microsoft rates as dangerous are blocked in all apps; a wrongly blocked site needs Restore or an exception. Windows Security then shows this setting as managed by your organisation.

rules.action: Block potentially unwanted apps
rules.reason: Microsoft Defender blocks adware, bundleware and other potentially unwanted apps when they download or install. Needs Microsoft Defender as the active antivirus.
rules.featureLoss: Some free programs that bundle offers or toolbars are blocked and quarantined. Windows Security then shows this setting as managed by your organisation.

rules.action: Run Defender's content scanning in a sandbox
rules.reason: Sets the machine variable MP_FORCE_USE_SANDBOX so Microsoft Defender runs its scanning processes in a sandbox, limiting what a compromised scanner could do.
rules.featureLoss: Takes effect after a restart; Defender may use slightly more memory.

rules.action: Run LSA as a protected process without UEFI lock
rules.reason: Protects the Local Security Authority, which holds sign-in secrets, from credential theft by code that is not signed for it. Pathweft sets the policy value without the UEFI lock, so Restore can turn it off again.
rules.featureLoss: Third-party sign-in plug-ins and drivers that are not signed for LSA protection stop loading, which can break smart-card, password manager or VPN sign-in. Takes effect after a restart.

rules.action: Do not run software supplied by the PC's firmware
rules.reason: The Windows Platform Binary Table lets PC firmware make Windows run a vendor program at every start, even after a clean install. Turning it off stops that program from being installed or reinstalled this way.
rules.featureLoss: Vendor anti-theft, support or driver utilities supplied through firmware are no longer installed by Windows. Takes effect after a restart.

rules.action: Turn off the PowerShell 2.0 optional feature
rules.reason: PowerShell 2.0 lacks the logging and script protections of later versions and can be used to bypass them. Recent Windows 11 builds no longer include it, so the rule shows as not present there.
rules.featureLoss: Scripts that explicitly start PowerShell -Version 2 stop working. Restore turns the feature back on from the files Windows keeps.

rules.action: Remove the deprecated WMIC capability
rules.reason: WMIC is deprecated and commonly used by malware to run commands and gather information; newer Windows builds no longer install it.
rules.featureLoss: Scripts and installers that call wmic.exe fail. Restore adds WMIC back through Windows Update and needs an internet connection.

rules.action: Remove the deprecated VBScript capability
rules.reason: VBScript is deprecated and a frequent malware delivery route; Microsoft plans to remove it from Windows.
rules.featureLoss: .vbs scripts, and installers or Office macros that use VBScript, stop working. Restore adds VBScript back through Windows Update and needs an internet connection.
